newsitem.title: USA: Portland Genl delays retail wheeling pilot.
newsitem.headline: Portland Genl delays retail wheeling pilot.

text.p: A request by Portland General Electric Co to delay review of a retail wheeling pilot was granted Wednesday by the Oregon Public Utilities Commission (OPUC), the company said.

The pilot was originally set to start April 1, but delays in a settlement of Portland's planned merger with Enron Corp have pushed the schedule for a decision by the OPUC back to at least May 1, a spokeswoman for the utility said.
The pilot is "tied to the merger and the merger has been delayed," she noted.
The OPUC earlier this week set June 4 as its deadline for deciding on the merger, which has been held up over disagreement on the amount of a rate cut for Oregon electricity ratepayers.
The utility filed in December a plan to allow large industrial customers to purchase up to a third of their load from other suppliers under the one-year pilot.

Last month, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) said the retail wheeling pilot did not meet rules for open access transmission, but the Portland General spokeswoman said that was a procedural issue unlikely to hold up the plan.
